"""Negative responses to short consonant-junction spelling fragments.

Look for a consonant followed by a labial spelling (w/v/m/f/b/p), either
across a token boundary or inside the current token. Transliteration lets
this rule cover Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and Georgian letters. Short fragments
are much stronger than long tokens; capitals are weaker. Pair strengths and
length discounts were fitted on training activations. Other responses,
including punctuation and spelling-specific exceptions, are not modeled.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import unicodedata
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()
CONSONANTS = set('bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz')
LABIALS = 'wvmfbp'

# Columns: w, v, m, f, b, p. Rows: internal pair; token-boundary pair.
RIGHT = (
    (1.554, 1.316, 0.196, 0.088, 0.369, 0.141),
    (2.342, 1.862, 0.387, 0.346, 0.751, 0.297),
)
# Previous letter: z; s; h/digraph; t/d/k/g/c/q; l/r; n/m; other.
LEFT = (
    (3.896, 1.712, 2.780, 1.0, 1.102, 0.292, 0.355),
    (2.305, 2.110, 2.548, 1.0, 0.756, 0.552, 0.568),
)
# Current token's letter count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5+.
LENGTH = (1.0, 0.4669, 0.1993, 0.0594, 0.0063)


@lru_cache(None)
def normalize(s):
    # Modern Greek beta is a v-like labial.
    return anyascii(s.replace('β', 'v').replace('Β', 'V')).lower()


@lru_cache(None)
def token_info(s):
    word = s.strip()
    scripts = ('LATIN', 'CYRILLIC', 'GREEK', 'GEORGIAN')
    valid = bool(word) and all(
        ch.isalpha() and any(k in unicodedata.name(ch, '') for k in scripts)
        for ch in word
    )
    text = normalize(s)
    upper = tuple(ch.isupper() for ch in s for _ in normalize(ch))
    cyrillic = any('CYRILLIC' in unicodedata.name(ch, '') for ch in word)
    return text, upper, len(word) if valid else 0, cyrillic


def previous_kind(text):
    if text.endswith(('sh', 'zh', 'ch', 'th')):
        return 2
    ch = text[-1:]
    for kind, letters in enumerate(('z', 's', 'h', 'tdkgcq', 'lr', 'nm')):
        if ch in letters:
            return kind
    return 6


def pair(info, previous):
    text, upper, n, cyrillic = info
    if not n or not text:
        return None
    # Prefer a junction spanning the token boundary.
    if (previous and previous[-1] in CONSONANTS
            and text[0] in LABIALS and previous[-1] != text[0]):
        return LABIALS.index(text[0]), previous_kind(previous), 1, upper[0]
    candidates = []
    for i in range(1, len(text)):
        if (text[i] in LABIALS and text[i-1] in CONSONANTS
                and text[i] != text[i-1]):
            candidates.append((LABIALS.index(text[i]),
                               previous_kind(text[:i]), 0, upper[i]))
    return min(candidates, key=lambda p: p[0]) if candidates else None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    info = token_info(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    junction = pair(info, previous)
    value = 0.0
    if junction:
        letter, left, boundary, upper = junction
        value = -RIGHT[boundary][letter] * LEFT[boundary][left]
        value *= LENGTH[min(info[2], 5) - 1]
        if upper:
            value *= 0.239
        if info[3]:
            value *= 1.698
    return (doc, (previous + info[0])[-4:]), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP neuron 2625, read through its down-projection component.

The component's input direction is dominated by MLP hidden neuron 2625 of layer 1 (about
70% of its squared norm, with the entry -0.98), so the component mostly tracks that neuron's
hidden value with the sign flipped: it goes NEGATIVE when the neuron fires. The neuron fires
on a voiced labial letter (w, v, в, б) that continues a word as a short piece right after
another letter piece of the same word, typically a rare name or foreign word that the
tokenizer splits into fragments, e.g. "Wiras|w|asta", "Ash|w|agandha", "Lud|v|onga",
"Mosk|va". Common words split the same way (e.g. "brain|w|ashed") give little. The neuron is
also slightly positive on the first token of each document.

Rule, per token (the carry is unused):
  * document start (first token of the row or of a new document): +0.2
  * otherwise, if the token is a bare letter fragment (no leading space, letters only) and
    the previous token is also letters only (same document):
      single letter w, в                    -2.2   (strongest)
      single letter v, б, В                 -1.2
      single letter b, m, f, п, м, W, Б, V  -0.3
      2-3 letters containing v, w or в      -0.25  (e.g. "va", "we", "ver")
  * everything else: 0.

Fitted on 6144 training rows (about 3.1M tokens) it explains about 14-15% of the variance
there, and 9% on the held-out eval rows (their large spikes are rarer). The biggest negative
spikes (-5 to -10) come from rare words the rule cannot see, so most of the variance stays
unexplained. What the rule keeps: the sign, the location (v/w/в-type letters inside split
words), and the typical size.
"""

READS = ()

STRONG = set("wв")
MEDIUM = set("vбВ")
WEAK = set("bmfпмWБV")
VW_LETTERS = set("vwVWвВ")
DOC_START = 0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    # the current token must continue a word: no leading space, letters only
    if not tok.isalpha() or tok[:1].isspace() or not prev.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    if len(tok) == 1:
        if tok in STRONG:
            return carry, -2.2
        if tok in MEDIUM:
            return carry, -1.2
        if tok in WEAK:
            return carry, -0.3
        return carry, 0.0
    if len(tok) <= 3 and any(c in VW_LETTERS for c in tok):
        return carry, -0.25
    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2626 — a "document opener" detector.

What it does
------------
This component is almost silent everywhere except at the first token of a document.
A document starts at the first token of a row and wherever the document id changes
(each document is preceded by <|endoftext|>). The model's attention never crosses a
document boundary, so that first token attends only to itself: its activation depends
on nothing but which token it is. Mid-document positions are near zero (|activation|
rarely above 0.5).

So the program predicts, at a document's first token, a value chosen by what kind of
token opens the document, and predicts 0 everywhere else:

  - a line break with a carriage return (CRLF, "\\r"): strongly negative (about -4.4)
  - a triple-quote block opener ('\"\"\"' or "'''"): strongly positive (about +3.6)
  - a bare capital letter with no leading space (A, B, Q, ...): positive (about +2.1)
  - a digit with no leading space (0-9): mildly positive (about +0.9)
  - code or markup openers with a symbol such as # { } < > \\ * /: mildly positive (about +0.5)
  - a word with a leading space (" of", " the", " for"...): mildly negative (about -0.5)
  - other capitalised words: about -0.25; lowercase words: about 0
  - punctuation-only tokens: about -0.5

The values are the mean activation of each group over document-opening tokens in the
training data, weighted by how often each token opens a document. This is a short rule
list, not a per-token table: it gets roughly a quarter of the variance at document
openers. A full per-token table (one value for each of the ~150k tokens, which is exact)
would explain much more, but it has no concept behind it.
"""

READS = ()

# Symbols that mark code or markup at the start of a document.
CODE_SYMBOLS = set("#{}<>\\*/")


def opener_value(token: str) -> float:
    """Predicted activation when `token` is the first token of a document."""
    bare = token.strip()
    leading_space = token[:1] == " "
    if "\r" in token:
        return -4.4  # CRLF line-break tokens
    if token.startswith('"""') or token.startswith("'''"):
        return 3.6  # triple-quote block openers
    if len(bare) == 1 and bare.isascii() and bare.isupper() and not leading_space:
        return 2.1  # a bare capital letter
    if bare.isdigit() and len(bare) == 1 and not leading_space:
        return 0.9  # a single digit
    if any(ch in CODE_SYMBOLS for ch in token):
        return 0.5  # code or markup symbol
    if leading_space and bare[:1].isalpha():
        return -0.5  # a word with a leading space
    if bare[:1].isupper() and bare.isascii():
        return -0.25  # other capitalised words
    if bare[:1].islower() and bare.isascii():
        return -0.05  # lowercase words
    if not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in token):
        return -0.5  # punctuation only
    return -0.25


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Called once per position. The first token of a document (the row's first token,
    or the first token after a change of document id) gets its opener value; every other
    position gets 0."""
    starts_document = (
        len(prefix.token_ids) == 1
        or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if not starts_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, float(opener_value(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

"""Estimate the response to letter-like mathematical labels in running text.

A short Latin/Greek symbol is most negative after the name of a quantity
("speed v", "integer n") or a variable-introducing word ("let x").
Formula delimiters also signal symbols; recent repetition weakens the response.
Ordinary a/I and bare letter fragments receive smaller background values.
There is an independent positive response to repeated middle dots.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import unicodedata
import wordnet

READS = ()
GREEK_NAMES = set('''alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa
lambda mu nu xi omicron pi rho sigma tau upsilon phi chi psi omega'''.split())
MOTION = set('speed velocity acceleration'.split())
DIMENSION = set('radius distance length width height depth altitude'.split())
PHYSICS = set('''mass force current momentum energy charge voltage potential
power density pressure temperature frequency wavelength time rate strength
permittivity resistivity
weight resistance capacitance inductance flux resistor lifetime'''.split())
MATH = set('''integer number ratio matrix function set vector relation variable
parameter coefficient constant exponent eigenvalue value size position
probability variance covariance deviation index degree order factor graph
subset region domain polynomial scalar root ring group sequence field metric
operator equation scale sum term coordinate signal input output'''.split())
GEOMETRY = set('''point line side angle vertex plane circle triangle
rectangle segment'''.split())
INTRODUCERS = set('let denote define suppose given assume consider where'.split())
QUANTIFIERS = set('each any all some every arbitrary'.split())
QUALIFIERS = set('''fixed positive negative odd even prime real complex possible
smallest largest maximum minimum'''.split())
GROUPS = ((MOTION, 4.8), (DIMENSION, 3.5), (PHYSICS, 2.8), (MATH, 2.2),
          (GEOMETRY, 1.0), (INTRODUCERS, 1.0), (QUANTIFIERS, 1.0),
          (QUALIFIERS, 1.0))


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def cue(word):
    word = word.strip(' ()[]{}:;,\"')
    forms = set(wordnet.base_forms(word, 'noun')) | {word.lower()}
    for group, strength in GROUPS:
        if forms & group:
            return strength
    return 0.1 if word.isalpha() and wordnet.is_a(word, 'quantity') else 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else []
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = token.strip()
    latin = len(text) == 1 and text.isascii() and text.isalpha()
    greek = (len(text) == 1 and text.isalpha()
             and 'GREEK' in unicodedata.name(text, ''))
    name = text.lower() in GREEK_NAMES
    value = 0.0
    if len(text) >= 2 and set(text) == {'·'}:
        value = 1.9
    elif latin or greek or name:
        spaced = token.startswith(' ')
        ordinary = text in {'a', 'I'}
        if ordinary:
            value = 0.0 if spaced else -0.055
        else:
            value = -0.11 if spaced else -0.015
        if greek:
            value = -0.26 if spaced else -0.02
        if name:
            value = -0.15
        if history:
            previous = history[-1].strip()
            markup = previous in {'$', '$\\', '\\(', '`', '$$', '\\'}
            bracket = previous in {'(', '[', '{'}
            strength = cue(previous)
            # A TeX command such as \times is not the noun "time".
            if len(history) > 1 and history[-2].endswith('\\'):
                strength = 0.0
            if len(history) > 1:
                earlier = cue(history[-2].strip())
                if markup:
                    strength += 0.7 * earlier
                if previous.lower() in {'of', 'the'}:
                    strength += 0.5 * earlier
            factor = 1.0 if spaced or greek or markup else 0.35
            ambiguous = previous.lower() in {'time', 'force', 'set'}
            if ordinary and (strength <= 1.0 or ambiguous):
                factor *= 0.4
            context = strength + 0.15 * (previous.isalpha() and len(previous) >= 5)
            context += 0.2 * markup + 0.32 * bracket
            repetition = sum(
                1.0 / lag for lag, old in enumerate(reversed(history), 1)
                if old.strip() == text
            )
            value += factor * (0.16 * repetition - context)
    return (doc, (history + [token])[-8:]), value

"""Predict human-participant cues from local English phrases and equivalents.

Negative values mostly mark a pending person/source/recipient: 'help from',
'work with', 'talk to', 'daughter of', or 'written by'. This is a lexical
semantic approximation, not a syntactic parser. Inflections come from WordNet.
Weak training-fitted corrections are omitted to keep the rules small.
"""
import re
import regex
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Each group collects words with a shared role in these constructions.
LEXICONS = {
    'message': 'email letter call fax message statement notification instruction '
        'advice recommendation report feedback news question response answer '
        'invitation request complaint notice correspondence comment information '
        'confirmation approval endorsement bid suggestion quote testimony',
    'speech': 'talk speak write communicate reply answer tell say explain '
        'report hear listen read learn inform notify reveal apologize',
    'transfer': 'receive obtain acquire buy purchase borrow steal get send give '
        'grant offer pay donate deliver award supply lend take provide download '
        'collect inherit fund loan money payment gift ticket',
    'help': 'help support assistance aid guidance expertise service protection '
        'care oversight supervision contribution permission consent attention',
    'joint': 'consult negotiate partner collaborate cooperate meet discuss chat '
        'interview converse conversation agreement contract appointment '
        'partnership collaboration cooperation discussion relation marriage',
    'work': 'work share trade invest deal engage interact join relationship '
        'connection contact border time',
    'personal': 'mind hand eye heart voice view perspective life home residence '
        'discretion behalf right interest effort concern need behaviour behavior '
        'attitude decision intention demand wish memory personality trait role '
        'leadership authority possession belonging credential activity action',
    'agent': 'write author produce develop create design found build invent '
        'publish direct compose record draw illustrate sign approve issue control '
        'require appoint elect capture discover introduce play represent make '
        'hold perform conduct provide lead operate manage organize own use adopt '
        'describe edit host teach submit purchase command review hire request '
        'endorse employ execute assign release present select fund prepare',
    'awareness': 'available accessible open known apparent obvious clear '
        'evident important seem appear prove',
}
GROUPS = {k: set(v.split()) for k, v in LEXICONS.items()}

@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def base_forms(word):
    return set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) | {word}


@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def concepts(word):
    forms = base_forms(word)
    found = {k for k, words in GROUPS.items() if forms & words}
    if forms & FAMILY:
        found.add('family')
    return found

FAMILY = set('father mother brother sister son daughter wife husband parent '
             'child uncle aunt nephew niece cousin grandson granddaughter '
             'grandfather grandmother sibling spouse widow widower'.split())
RECEIPT = set('receive obtain seek hear'.split())

FOREIGN = {
    'source': set('von fra från от _from'.split()),
    'with': set('con mit с avec com'.split()),
    'of': set('de di du des del của'.split()),
    'to': set('向 给 給 à'.split()),
    'for': set('für для'.split()),
    'at_person': set('bei у'.split()),
    'agent': {'由'},
    'let_person': {'让', '讓'},
}
ADDRESS = set('contact notify interview inform convince persuade invite '
              'thank greet congratulate reassure warn remind'.split())
HUMAN_OBJECT_VERBS = set('hire employ marry appoint assist'.split())
FLEXIBLE_OBJECT_VERBS = set('teach tell ask approach visit join accompany '
                           'meet arrest kill'.split())
PREPOSITIONS = set('from with to of by between among against '
                   'alongside amongst'.split())
# Additive adjustments for the named lexical and construction cues.
WEIGHTS = {
    'address': -0.592,
    'human_object': -0.767,
    'flexible_object': -0.214,
    'passive': 0.165,
    'verb_frame': -0.366,
    'noun_frame': 0.133,
    'against': -0.049,
    'against:agent': -0.33,
    'alongside': -0.514,
    'among': -0.895,
    'amongst': -0.751,
    'between': -0.342,
    'between:speech': -0.357,
    'between:joint': -1.034,
    'by': -0.378,
    'by:message': -0.303,
    'by:transfer': -0.317,
    'by:agent': -0.777,
    'from': -0.576,
    'from:message': -1.322,
    'from:speech': -0.532,
    'from:transfer': -1.03,
    'from:help': -1.721,
    'of': -0.032,
    'of:message': -0.411,
    'of:help': -1.169,
    'of:work': -0.386,
    'of:personal': -0.79,
    'of:family': -1.235,
    'to': -0.074,
    'to:message': -0.526,
    'to:speech': -0.977,
    'to:transfer': -0.815,
    'to:awareness': -0.786,
    'to:attribution': -0.55,
    'with': -0.171,
    'with:speech': -1.1,
    'with:joint': -2.756,
    'with:work': -1.013,
    'from:receipt': -1.406,
    'foreign:source': -0.358,
    'foreign:with': -0.184,
    'foreign:of': -0.106,
    'foreign:to': -0.376,
    'foreign:for': -0.098,
    'foreign:at_person': -0.569,
    'foreign:agent': -0.671,
    'foreign:let_person': -0.562,
}


def features(current, text):
    """Find active cues using only this token and recent preceding text."""
    word = current.strip().lower()
    f = {}
    # Ignore word-internal alphabetic fragments, except Han characters.
    if (current[:1].isalpha() and text[-1:].isalnum()
            and not regex.match(r'\p{Script=Han}', current)):
        return f
    for name, words in FOREIGN.items():
        if word in words:
            f['foreign:' + name] = 1.0
    previous_words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', text[-80:])
    prev = previous_words[-1].lower() if previous_words else ''
    context_word = prev
    adverb = prev.endswith('ly') and 'adverb' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(prev)
    if len(previous_words) > 1 and (adverb or prev in
            {'up', 'out', 'back', 'more', 'together'}):
        context_word = previous_words[-2].lower()
    if word in PREPOSITIONS:
        f[word] = 1.0
        if word == 'from' and any(base_forms(w.lower()) & RECEIPT
                                   for w in previous_words[-7:]):
            f['from:receipt'] = 1.0
        for name in concepts(context_word):
            f[word + ':' + name] = 1.0
        if prev == 'according':
            f[word + ':attribution'] = 1.0
    if word.isalpha():
        forms = base_forms(word)
        if forms & ADDRESS:
            f['address'] = 1.0
        if forms & HUMAN_OBJECT_VERBS:
            f['human_object'] = 1.0
        if forms & FLEXIBLE_OBJECT_VERBS:
            f['flexible_object'] = 1.0
        if forms & (ADDRESS | HUMAN_OBJECT_VERBS | FLEXIBLE_OBJECT_VERBS):
            if prev in ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'be', 'been', 'being'):
                f['passive'] = 1.0
            if prev in ('to', 'please', 'can', 'may', 'could', 'will', 'would',
                        'should', 'must', 'not'):
                f['verb_frame'] = 1.0
            if prev in ('a', 'an', 'the', 'your', 'his', 'my', 'their'):
                f['noun_frame'] = 1.0
    return f


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    current = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    f = features(current, text)
    value = sum((WEIGHTS.get(k, 0.0) * v for k, v in f.items()), 0.0)
    return (doc, (text + current)[-120:]), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2628 -- a "person-directed preposition" detector.

What it does: this component goes negative on a preposition (to, with, from, by, of,
among, between, against) when the word before it is a verb or noun of dealing with
people: talk to, wrote to, sent to, given to, contact with, collaborated with, request
from, help from, assistance of, son of. Those prepositions are about to name a person,
group or organisation. Elsewhere the preposition is only mildly negative, and on
infinitive "to" (need to, able to, how to) or "compatible with / corresponding to /
proof of" it is about zero. The words "contact", "married", "appointed", "meet",
"interview" and "relationship(s)" are themselves mildly negative.

Predictions are in the component's own units (the activation), so a negative number
means the component is pushing against its usual direction at that token.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation of each preposition when no special context applies.
PREP = {"to": -0.1, "with": -0.3, "from": -0.6, "by": -0.45, "of": -0.05,
        "against": -0.6, "among": -0.8, "between": -0.4}

# Typical activation of the same preposition after a person-dealing word.
PERSON_PREP = {"to": -1.2, "with": -1.2, "from": -2.5, "by": -1.0, "of": -0.9,
               "among": -1.0, "between": -0.6, "against": -1.0}

# Verbs and nouns of communication, transfer, contact and partnership.
PERSON_WORDS = set("""talk talked talking speak spoke speaking write wrote writing letter send sent
sending sell sold give gave given provide provided providing available contact contacted
contacting meet met married marry appoint appointed assist assistance help helped relationship
relationships collaborate collaborated collaboration working worked work interact interacts
interview invited invite notify reply replied request requests ask asked appeal report reported
explain seek sue engage partner partnered agree deal dealing connection share shares approached
responded obtained received receive taken take comes come call called information services
service made present presented known according border""".split())

# People, and nouns whose complement is usually a person ("son of", "attention of").
PEOPLE = set("""son daughter father mother wife husband friend friends team coach people men women
children family members interests assistance attention eyes minds hands opinion voices residence
discretion those needs help support""".split())

# Prepositions in "compatible with", "corresponding to", "proof of", "effects of": not a person.
MATCH = set("""compatible compared consistent corresponding corresponds correspond related unrelated
proof author tour effects effect parts portion range ranging part""".split())

# Words before an infinitive "to": need to, able to, how to, try to.
INFINITIVE = set("""need needs want wants wanted able how try trying going unable like decided is has
have not easy hard difficult likely sure time way order""".split())

# Words that are themselves mildly negative.
PERSON_TOKENS = set("""contact married appointed relationships relationship meet interview assist""".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return carry, 0.0
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    if tok in PERSON_TOKENS:
        return carry, -0.8
    if tok not in PREP:
        return carry, 0.0
    if prev in MATCH:
        return carry, 0.0
    if tok == "to" and prev in INFINITIVE:
        return carry, 0.0
    if prev in PERSON_WORDS or prev in PEOPLE:
        return carry, PERSON_PREP[tok]
    return carry, PREP[tok]

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2629 (a small, mostly unexplained piece).

Its activation is near 0 almost everywhere (std ~0.05) with rare spikes. Two
things here account for what is predictable:

1. Document starts. The first token of a document (or of a packed row), which the
   model sees with no preceding text, gets a small negative value when it is a
   mid-sentence fragment (lowercase word or a token with a leading space), and a
   small positive value when it is CJK or other wide script.
2. Web-page furniture. Words that open page chrome or forum boilerplate
   (" Latest", " Explanation", " Details", " Related", "Title", ...) get a
   negative value when they occur mid-document; they are the strongest
   negative spikes in the data, though not reliable (median near 0).

Everything else predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Page-furniture words, as the tokenizer splits them (leading space included).
FURNITURE = {
    " Explanation", " Latest", " Details", " Updated", "Title", " Last", " Results",
    " Related", " Replies", " Reply", " Questions", " Article", " Online", " Topics",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2630 - a "len" detector.

This component writes a large negative value into the residual stream whenever the
text being read spells out "len": the Python builtin `len` (as in `len(x)`, `= len`,
`strlen`), the word "length" and its forms, and names such as Ellen or Helene where
"len" or "lene" is split across word pieces. It is near zero on everything else.

The program reads the token being predicted (and the token before it, to catch a
"len" split across two pieces, e.g. "Coll" + "en") and returns a fixed value per
case, the average activation the component shows in that case on training text:

  - the token is exactly "len"                       -> -6.1  (strongest)
  - the token is "length", "lens", "lengths", ...    -> -1.7
  - a short "en..." piece right after a piece ending in "l" (Coll|en, hel|ene)
                                                     -> -2.8
  - a short piece ending in "len" (elen, ellen)      -> -2.7
  - Russian "лен" / "Ленин", Chinese "长度"           -> -2.3 / -1.8
  - anything else                                    ->  0
"""
import re

READS = ()


def _letters(text):
    """Lowercase letters only: ' (len' -> 'len', 'Coll' -> 'coll'."""
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", text.lower())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = _letters(cur)
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = _letters(prefix.token_strings[-2]) if same_doc else ""
    if word == "len":
        value = -6.1
    elif word.startswith("len"):
        value = -1.7
    elif word.startswith("en") and len(word) <= 4 and prev.endswith("l"):
        value = -2.8
    elif word.endswith("len") and len(word) <= 5:
        value = -2.7
    elif cur.strip().lower() in ("лен", "ленин"):
        value = -2.3
    elif "长度" in cur:
        value = -1.8
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Name-linking particles, approximated from the preceding noun.

`of` is positive after people, titles and names, but negative after physical
measurements and life/birth/death. Other origin particles, Roman suffixes,
and epithet-introducing articles share the personal-name cues. WordNet noun classes,
capitalization and word frequency provide crude name detection.
All other tokens receive zero. Only the preceding two words are examined.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
MEASUREMENTS = set("length width height depth size weight distance position "
                   "location age duration magnitude angle velocity speed".split())
PEOPLE = set("person people man men woman women human humans folk folks personnel".split())
PARTICLES = set("from de del della di da des von du van dos das".split())
ROMAN = set("I II III IV V VI VII VIII IX X".split())
WORD = re.compile(r"([^\W\d_]+)$")


@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def word_scores(word):
    cats = wordnet.categories(word, 'noun')
    bases = set(wordnet.base_forms(word, 'noun')) | {word.lower()}
    cap = word[:1].isupper()
    person = 'noun.person' in cats
    # All noun senses fall in the person category (not contextual parsing).
    person_only = person and len(cats) == 1
    personal_noun = person and 'verb' not in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    named = cap and person
    clear_name = cap and person_only
    unknown = cap and not cats
    rare_name = unknown and zipf_frequency(word, 'en') < 3.5
    noble = wordnet.is_a(word, 'aristocrat')
    royal = wordnet.is_a(word, 'sovereign')
    clergy = wordnet.is_a(word, 'clergyman')
    leader = wordnet.is_a(word, 'leader')
    people = bool(bases & PEOPLE)
    vital = bool(bases & {'life', 'birth', 'death'})
    of = (.2 + .5*cap + 1.2*person_only + 1.1*named + 1.5*rare_name
          + .3*personal_noun + 2*noble + 2*royal + 1.5*clergy + .3*leader
          + 4*people - bool(bases & MEASUREMENTS)
          - bool(bases & {'speed', 'velocity'}) - 3.2*vital)
    particle = (.1 + .5*cap + .6*person_only + .9*clear_name
                + .25*personal_noun + .2*unknown + .4*leader + 3.2*noble
                + .8*royal + 1.8*people - .4*vital)
    roman = (.8*named + 1.7*clear_name + 2*rare_name + .35*personal_noun
             + 5.5*royal + .7*leader + .5*noble)
    article = (2.3*clear_name + .3*named + .8*rare_name
               + .55*personal_noun + 5.4*royal + .4*leader)
    return of, particle, roman, article


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else b''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    carry = (doc, (previous + prefix.token_bytes[-1])[-160:])
    lower = token.strip().lower()
    if lower == 'of':
        column = 0
    elif lower in PARTICLES:
        column = 1
    elif token.startswith(' ') and token.strip() in ROMAN:
        column = 2
    elif lower in {'the', 'le', 'la'}:
        column = 3
    elif lower in {'aus', 'din'}:
        return carry, .9
    else:
        return carry, 0.0
    text = previous.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    match = WORD.search(text)
    word = match[1] if match else ''
    value = word_scores(word)[column]
    before = text[:match.start()] if match else text
    earlier = re.search(r"([^\W\d_]+)\s+$", before)
    if earlier and earlier[1][:1].isupper():
        value += (.3, .25, .15, 0)[column]
    return carry, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2631 -- the "of-phrase inside a name or title" feature.

What it does: this component fires on the small connecting word ("of", "de", "from",
"von", ...) that joins a title, office, people, or organisation to what follows it, as in
"Earl of ...", "Bishop of ...", "people of ...", "member of ...", "Republic of ...", or
"Frederick de ...". Its output pushes the next-token guess toward place and organisation
names. It is almost silent everywhere else.

How this program predicts it: at each token, if the token is such a connecting word, look
at the word just before it and grade the strength by what kind of word that is:
  - a rank, office, or noble/clerical title ("Earl", "Bishop", "President"): strong
  - a people, body, or place word ("people", "Republic", "Court", "county"): medium-strong
  - a comma right after a capitalised name ("Michael Kogan, of ..."): strong
  - any other capitalised word (a name): medium
  - an amount or measure ("number of", "one of", "speed of"): zero
  - any other lower-case word: weak
Everything else predicts 0. Values are the group means measured on training text.

What it misses: most of the variance sits in the weak group ("of" after an ordinary
noun), where which noun comes before "of" matters in ways no short word list captures.
"""

READS = ()

CONNECTORS = {
    "of", "Of", "OF", "de", "De", "DE", "von", "Von", "from", "aus", "di", "della", "del",
    "da", "z", "d", "van", "des",

    "earl", "duke", "count", "countess", "bishop", "archbishop", "prince", "princess", "king",
    "queen", "emperor", "lord", "baron", "baroness", "viscount", "knight", "ruler", "regent",
    "governor", "mayor", "minister", "senator", "chancellor", "secretary", "judge", "clerk",
    "general", "director", "cardinal", "chief", "commander", "captain", "sheikh", "sultan",
    "pope", "abbot", "dean", "chairman", "professor", "coach", "member", "author", "owner",
    "leader", "emperors",
}

# Groups of people, bodies and places: "people of", "Republic of", "Court of".
PEOPLE_AND_PLACES = {
    "people", "citizens", "citizen", "residents", "natives", "men", "women", "workers",
    "personnel", "children", "players", "player", "band", "team", "party", "state", "states",
    "republic", "kingdom", "empire", "country", "court", "board", "bank", "department",
    "school", "university", "society", "union", "league", "order", "legion", "knights", "act",
    "treaty", "council", "army", "church", "diocese", "county", "city", "town", "district",
    "region", "province", "island", "islands", "valley", "gulf", "bay", "river", "economy",
    "population", "capital", "government", "ministry", "academy",
}

# Amounts, parts and measures: "number of", "one of", "value of", "speed of".
AMOUNTS = {
    "one", "all", "each", "some", "any", "many", "number", "out", "part", "instance", "lot",
    "value", "use", "range", "case", "result", "end", "effects", "process", "development",
    "portion", "sum", "side", "piece", "kind", "variety", "most", "more", "half", "rest",
    "sequence", "%", "speed", "height", "distance", "length", "position", "location", "time",
    "place", "amount", "rate", "size", "date", "color", "view", "type", "form", "way", "set",
    "product", "members",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """This position's predicted activation: strength of a connecting word after a title,
    people/place word, name, or comma-after-name; zero for amounts and other tokens."""
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.0
    if prefix.token_strings[-1].strip() not in CONNECTORS:
        return None, 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    low = prev.lower()
    if low in TITLES:
        return None, 1.9
    if low in PEOPLE_AND_PLACES:
        return None, 1.4
    if low in AMOUNTS:
        return None, 0.0
    if prev == "," and len(prefix.token_strings) > 2 and prefix.token_strings[-3].strip()[:1].isupper():
        return None, 1.6
    if prev[:1].isupper():
        return None, 0.75
    return None, 0.2

"""Repeated person names in prose (layer-1 MLP unit 2633, down_proj component).

The unit responds to the tokens of a proper name (a capitalized word, or a later
sub-word piece of one) once that name has already appeared earlier in the same
document: a character or person being mentioned again. It stays near zero on first
mentions, on common capitalized words (The, If, Let, This...), on all-caps code
identifiers, and on ordinary text. Its response is larger in running prose (many
lowercase words in the last 50 tokens) than in code, lists or headings.

Prediction: GAIN * (share of lowercase words in the last 50 tokens) on a repeated
name piece, 0 elsewhere. Each document starts fresh, as the model's attention does.
"""

READS = ()

GAIN = 0.6
WINDOW = 50

# Capitalized words that are common English (function words, sentence openers), not names.
COMMON = frozenset(
    """The A An I In On At This That These Those It Its He She We They You His Her Our Their
    So If And But As For To Of Or What When Where Who Which Why How Let Wait Thus Therefore
    Alternatively Also Hmm No Yes Is Are Was Were All None True False Time Data Test Error
    Result Download Type List Line Figure Table Note Okay Oh Well Now Then There Here Please
    Thanks Dear Hello Hi Do Does Did Can Could Will Would Should May Might Must Not Only Just
    Even Still Yet After Before Since While Although Because Once Until Unless Though Whether
    Other Some Many Most Each Every Any Both Either Neither Such More Less Very Much Few""".split()
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "seen": set(), "word": "", "prose": []}
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    piece = tok.strip()
    # A word starts at a token with a leading space or newline, or after punctuation.
    starts_word = tok[:1] in (" ", "\n", "\t") or not tok[:1].isalpha()
    word = "" if starts_word else carry["word"]
    word = word + piece if piece.isalpha() else ""
    is_name = word[:1].isupper() and word not in COMMON and not word.isupper()
    seen = carry["seen"]
    repeat = is_name and (word in seen or (len(word) > 1 and any(s.startswith(word) for s in seen)))
    prose = carry["prose"]
    share = sum(prose) / len(prose) if prose else 0.5
    if is_name:
        seen.add(word)
    prose.append(piece.islower())
    del prose[:-WINDOW]
    value = GAIN * share if repeat else 0.0
    return {"doc": doc, "seen": seen, "word": word, "prose": prose}, value

"""Approximate a purpose-and-benefit action signal.

Uses dictionary meanings for improvement, prevention, protection,
achievement, assistance, and assessment in English and Chinese.
Explicit purpose markers increase the estimate. Chinese purpose context
stays active up to
64 tokens, unless Chinese sentence punctuation or a newline ends it. Dictionary
lookups also recognize traditional spellings and completed two-character
Chinese words. Separate rules cover initial "Title:" headings and repeated
middle-dot leaders. Many token-specific strength differences are omitted.
"""
import re
import regex
from functools import lru_cache
import cedict
import opencc
import wordnet

SIMPLE = opencc.OpenCC('t2s')
GROUPS = (
    set(
        'improve enhance strengthen bolster reinforce boost advance promote '
        'further optimize perfect refine facilitate develop deepen raise '
        'heighten elevate upgrade increase augment expand enlarge intensify '
        'enrich '
    .split()),
    set(
        'reduce decrease lower lessen diminish minimize limit save spare '
        'avoid prevent avert preclude stop inhibit restrain curb eliminate '
        'eradicate remove relieve alleviate mitigate suppress combat '
        'counteract offset '
    .split()),
    set(
        'ensure guarantee secure safeguard protect preserve maintain defend '
        'sustain retain '
    .split()),
    set(
        'achieve attain accomplish realize fulfil fulfill satisfy meet '
        'reach complete solve resolve overcome implement execute establish '
        'build create consolidate adapt '
    .split()),
    set(
        'help assist aid support enable allow encourage empower guide lead '
        'foster cultivate train educate '
    .split()),
    set(
        'understand comprehend learn study assess evaluate examine '
        'investigate analyze analyse explore clarify identify determine '
        'test verify check demonstrate illustrate prove '
    .split()),
    set(
        'improve enhance strengthen bolster reinforce optimize perfect '
        'refine upgrade deepen enrich '
    .split()),
    set(
        'avoid prevent avert preclude thwart forestall '
    .split()),
)
EMPHASIS = (
    "进一步", "切实", "扎实", "充分", "积极",
    "有效", "大力", "更好地",
    "更好", "全面", "努力", "加快", "不断", "深入", "着力", "真正",
    "尽快", "牢固",
)


@lru_cache(None)
def describe(token, previous=""):
    """Read action meanings from WordNet and Chinese dictionary glosses."""
    text = token.strip()
    en = bool(re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]+", text))
    cn = bool(regex.search(r"\p{Script=Han}", text))
    flags = [0] * len(GROUPS)
    verb = bare = emphasis = False
    if en:
        word = text.lower()
        bases = wordnet.base_forms(word, "verb")
        bare = word in bases
        verb = "verb" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
        for base in bases:
            for i, meanings in enumerate(GROUPS):
                flags[i] |= base in meanings
    if cn:
        text = SIMPLE.convert(text)
        if len(text) == len(previous.strip()) == 1:
            combined = SIMPLE.convert(previous.strip()) + text
            if any(g.startswith("to ") for g in cedict.glosses(combined)):
                text = combined
        for modifier in EMPHASIS:
            if text.startswith(modifier):
                emphasis = True
                if len(text) > len(modifier):
                    text = text[len(modifier):]
                break
        for gloss in cedict.glosses(text):
            match = re.match(r"to (?:make |become )?([a-z]+)", gloss)
            if match:
                verb = True
                for i, meanings in enumerate(GROUPS):
                    flags[i] |= match[1] in meanings
        bare = verb
    return [en, cn, verb, bare, emphasis, len(text) == 1, *flags]

READS = ()

# Columns: Chinese base, single-character, English bare, inflected,
# English after "to", Chinese purpose-clause increment.
ACTION_WEIGHTS = (
    (0.252, -0.267, -0.011, -0.039, 0.21, 0.126),  # improve
    (0.144, -0.184, -0.012, -0.024, 0.135, 0.058),  # reduce
    (0.205, -0.219, -0.008, -0.005, 0.086, 0.844),  # ensure
    (0.162, -0.174, 0.019, -0.018, 0.058, 0.302),  # achieve
    (-0.003, 0.002, -0.03, -0.011, 0.077, -0.328),  # help
    (0.012, -0.003, -0.012, -0.007, -0.05, -0.083),  # assess
    (0.245, -0.258, 0.053, 0.029, 0.112, 0.503),  # quality
    (0.165, 0.076, 0.068, 0.001, 0.342, -0.253),  # prevention
)

BOUNDARY_PUNCTUATION = (
    '，。；：、？！“”‘’（）()['
    ']~ \n"\'.,:;!?'
)

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, before_previous, age, position = "", "", 1000, 0
        reset = True
    else:
        _, previous, before_previous, age, position = carry
        position += 1
        reset = False
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    alone = describe(token)
    description = (describe(token, previous)
                   if alone[1] and alone[5] and len(previous) == 1 else alone)
    en, cn, verb, bare, emphasis, single, *classes = description
    completed = description != alone
    goal = any(classes)
    to = previous in {"to", "To"}
    capital_to = previous == "To"
    order_to = to and before_previous in {
        "order", "effort", "as", "need", "attempt"
    }
    help_before = previous in {"help", "Help"}
    wei = previous in {"为", "為"} or (
        completed and before_previous in {"为", "為"}
    )
    purpose_markers = {"为了", "為了", "以便", "以期", "旨在"}
    weile = previous in purpose_markers or (
        completed and before_previous in purpose_markers
    )
    modal = previous in {
        "能", "可以", "能够", "要", "需", "需要", "必须", "应",
        "应该", "能夠", "應", "應該"
    }
    scope = max(0.0, 1.0 - age / 64)
    value = -0.002 + 0.001 * cn + 0.002 * en - 0.063 * reset
    for flag, weights in zip(classes, ACTION_WEIGHTS):
        cb, cs, eb, ei, et, cp = weights
        value += flag * cn * (cb + cs * single + cp * scope)
        value += flag * en * ((eb if bare else ei) + et * bare * to)
    if cn:
        value += verb * (
            0.019 + 0.361 * wei + 0.740 * weile
            + 0.012 * scope + 0.057 * modal
        )
        value += emphasis * (
            0.236 - 0.042 * scope + 0.385 * modal + 0.281 * goal
        )
        value += goal * (
            wei * (0.762 + 2.999 * (1 - single))
            + weile * (0.812 + 0.987 * (1 - single))
        )
    if en and bare:
        value += verb * (
            -0.001 * to + 0.108 * capital_to
            + 0.046 * order_to + 0.020 * help_before
        )
        value += goal * (
            0.482 * capital_to + 0.210 * order_to + 0.092 * help_before
        )
    if word.lower() in {"further", "better", "best"} and to:
        value += 0.418
    if (word.startswith("为了") or word.startswith("為了")) and len(word) > 2:
        value += 1.587
    if position == 0 and word == "Title":
        value += -0.284
    if word == ":" and previous == "Title" and position == 1:
        value += 6.327
    if len(word) > 1 and set(word) == {"·"}:
        value += 0.300
    if any(ch in token for ch in "。！？；\n"):
        age = 1000
    cue = word.strip(BOUNDARY_PUNCTUATION) or word
    if cue in purpose_markers | {"为", "為"}:
        age = 0
    return (doc, cue, previous, age + 1, position), float(value)

after a purpose cue, as in "为了[保证]", "为[实现]", "to [avoid]", "进一步[提高]", or a

)

    "to": 0.2, " to": 0.2, "To": 0.2, " To": 0.2,               # English infinitive of purpose

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

What it does: the model splits rare or foreign words into pieces ("Rep|ar|atur",
"Steuer|er", "Av|ror|in"). This component fires on a piece that continues the current word
(no leading space) and contains the letter r (Latin r, Cyrillic р, Arabic ر), when the piece
just before it in the same word also contained an r. The response is strongest for short
vowel+r syllables ("er", "ar", "ir", "or", "ur", "ere", "era", ...) and roughly halves for

"Steuer|er". Anything else predicts 0.

"""Approximate a document-initial, spelling-sensitive transient.

Later tokens receive a near-zero prediction. At a row/document start,
add scores for token length, letters, common letter combinations,
quotation marks, indentation, and English coordinating conjunctions. These are
coarse spelling correlations, not a claim that the component represents
these words' meanings; irregular lexical responses remain unexplained.
"""

READS = ()
COORDINATING_CONJUNCTIONS = frozenset("and but for nor or so yet".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    first = prefix.position == 0 or (
        prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if not first:
        return None, 0.001
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().lower()
    value = -0.36 + 0.1810 * min(len(word), 15)
    value += -8.13 * bool(
        word and not any(c.isalnum() for c in word)
        and any(c in word for c in "'‘’")
    )
    value += -1.94 * bool(word.startswith('c'))
    value += 3.03 * bool(word in COORDINATING_CONJUNCTIONS)
    value += 4.27 * bool(any(c in word for c in '"“”'))
    value += 1.23 * bool('er' in word)
    value += 3.16 * bool(word.startswith('j'))
    value += -1.32 * bool('u' in word)
    value += 2.66 * bool(word.startswith('st'))
    value += 2.38 * bool(word.endswith('k'))
    value += 0.65 * bool('n' in word)
    value += -0.85 * bool('i' in word)
    value += 1.01 * bool(word.endswith('t'))
    value += -2.73 * bool(

    )

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2646 -- a document-start, word-class detector.

What it does: this component is almost silent except on the FIRST token of each
document (the first token after a document break, or the first token of a row). There
attention cannot see any earlier text, so its activation depends only on which word or
token that is. The program therefore predicts 0 everywhere except at document starts,
and there it returns a value chosen by the class of the token's word:

  * places, facilities and storage nouns (hospital, airport, warehouse, park)   +6.5
  * people / role nouns (person, guest, visitor, doctor, worker)               +6
  * greetings and interjections (hello, hi, please, here, just)                +5.5
  * double quote marks (" and curly quotes)                                    +4.4
  * quantifiers (many, some, more, other, various)                             +3
  * computing and data-structure terms (heap, stack, socket, JSON, string)     +2
  * conjunctions (and, or, but, that, as, if, when)                            +2
  * indentation runs (3+ spaces, or tabs)                                      -2.4
  * abstract nouns (idea, truth, love, freedom, theory)                        -2
  * colour words (red, blue, green, ...)                                       -3.5
  * prepositions (with, by, on, from, at, ...) and possessives (my, your, our)  -2.5 / -3
  * single quote marks and their fragments                                     -6
  * word-start fragments with a C/cl/cr/tw/sw onset (cl, cr, cu, Co, Pri)      -9
  * anything else                                                              0

What it does not capture: which particular nouns fire. Within "word" classes the
activation spreads widely (sd about 3), and a full per-token table would reach about
0.92 of the variance at document starts; these word classes reach about 0.17.

READS is empty: this is a stand-alone predictor.
"""

import re

READS = ()

PLACES = set("""hospital hotel airport park forest factory store shop restaurant warehouse bank school
campus office station market mall prison kitchen garage library museum church stadium arena plaza
lodge hostel clinic depot dock harbor harbour farm mine yard island city town village house home room
hall port parking cellar tavern pub cafe bar gym theatre theater cinema embassy palace castle temple
lab laboratory studio workshop inventory stock boutique supermarket pharmacy terminal hangar lounge
dormitory apartment motel resort casino college university academy hospice jail cemetery field""".split())

PEOPLE = set("""person people guest visitor customer client doctor patient employee worker staff
gentleman lady hand job manager man woman child user member citizen artist artisan passenger driver
teacher student lawyer officer soldier owner""".split())

COMPUTING = set("""word string char byte bytes pointer socket stack heap queue array list linkedlist
arraylist hashset hashmap dictionary map set buffer node tree record records token handle terminal
console server port memory cursor address static json xml sql html unix linux desktop hardware software
database stream file filesystem directory object class method variable function module package
interface docker kernel process thread pipe packet protocol url http api endpoint""".split())

COLOURS = set("red blue green yellow black white pink purple orange brown gray grey gold silver".split())

ABSTRACT = set("idea truth love hope fear freedom justice power law rule theory concept".split())

FRAGMENTS = set("cl cu cr cy tw sw su ly cle cla clo cre cri cur con com cou club cube coach cub coat colour cool".split())

PREPOSITIONS = set("""with by on de la from at be under upon into about over without among through
against between after before during like""".split())

POSSESSIVES = set("my your our his her their its".split())

CONJUNCTIONS = set("and or but that as if so because while when than".split())

GREETINGS = set("hello hi hey please thanks yes no here well oh okay ok just so".split())

QUANTIFIERS = set("many some most more other various several few all any each every both much".split())


def word_value(token: str) -> float:
    """The predicted activation for a document-starting token, by its word class."""
    m = re.fullmatch(r" ?([A-Za-z]+)", token)
    if m is None:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\s{3,}|\t\s*", token):
            return -2.4
        if "'" in token:
            return -6.0
        if '"' in token or "“" in token:
            return 4.4
        return 0.0
    w = m.group(1).lower()
    if w in PLACES:
        return 6.5
    if w in PEOPLE:
        return 6.0
    if w in COLOURS:
        return -3.5
    if w in FRAGMENTS:
        return -9.0
    if w in POSSESSIVES:
        return -3.0
    if w in PREPOSITIONS:
        return -2.5
    if w in GREETINGS:
        return 5.5
    if w in CONJUNCTIONS:
        return 2.0
    if w in QUANTIFIERS:
        return 3.0
    if w in COMPUTING:
        return 2.0
    if w in ABSTRACT:
        return -2.0
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    if not starts_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, float(word_value(prefix.token_strings[t]))

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2647: a "bone" spelling detector.

It goes strongly negative on the token that completes or continues the word
"bone" (bone, bones, bony, boning, debone, backbone, ...) and on the Chinese or
Japanese character 骨 (bone), and more weakly negative on the start of other
bon-/bond-/bow- spellings (Bon, bon, bond, bow, Bod). It is slightly positive on
the interpunct pair '··'. Everything else is 0.

The word-so-far is the letters since the last non-letter (or document start),
lower-cased, so "b" + "one" is recognised as "bone" and so on.
"""

# Activation for each word-so-far (lower-case letters since the last break).
BONE_WORDS = ("bone", "bones", "bony", "boning", "debone", "deboning", "backbone")
BON_STARTS = {"bon": -5.5, "bond": -1.6, "bow": -2.6, "bod": -3.3, "bonds": -1.0}

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = "" if carry is None else carry
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) > 1 and ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        word = ""  # a new document starts: the word resets
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if "骨" in token:
        return "", -9.0
    if token == "··":
        return "", 1.6
    for ch in token:
        word = word + ch.lower() if ch.isalpha() else ""
    if word in BONE_WORDS or word.endswith(("bone", "bones", "bony", "boning")):
        value = -9.0
    elif word in BON_STARTS:
        value = BON_STARTS[word]
    elif word.endswith("debon"):
        value = -8.0
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return word, value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2648 - a "J-name fragment" detector.

What it does: it reads the word being typed, token by token, and fires on the
token that completes a J-initial name fragment. The strongest case is "Jones"
(and "ones" right after a lone "J" token, as in "J" + "ones"). Next come
"Jan", "Jon", "Jane", "Joan", "Jun", "Jung", "Jong", and "jan"/"jun" inside
longer names such as "Ramanujan", "Arjun" or "Dijon". Ordinary J-words such
as June, January, junior, junction, jungle and Janet stay near zero. Fragments
with "ji" (Jig, Jiu, Jive, ...) push the other way, negative. The token ".com"
gets a weak positive value. Everything else is zero.

Why it is written this way: the activation is almost entirely a function of
which J-fragment has just been completed. A bare "J" right before the fragment
strengthens it. The values are in the component's own units: about +9 at most,
about -8 at least.

Limits: this captures about 15% of the variance on held-out text, and the eval
run agrees (variance explained about 0.2). The rest is spread over many single
words and context effects that a short rule does not express. A full
word-by-word table reaches only about 0.3, so this is near what a lexical rule
can get.

Program: `step` keeps the current word (lowercased) in the carry, restarting at
spaces, punctuation, and document starts. It returns the value for the newest
token.
"""

import re

READS = ()

JONES = re.compile(r"jones")
JXN = re.compile(r"j[oau]n")  # jan, jon, jun, jane, joan, juan, jung, jong
JI = re.compile(r"ji")  # jig, jiu, jive, ...

# Whole words that look like J-name fragments but do not fire.
NOT_NAMES = {
    "june", "january", "junior", "junction", "conjunction", "injunction",
    "adjunct", "jungle", "jonathan", "janet", "janeiro", "janvier", "jonah",
    "jonas", "junto", "juntos", "jangan", "junit", "django", "azerbaijan",
}

# Activation levels (component units): plain fragment, then after a lone "J".
JONES_VALUE, JONES_LONE = 4.5, 9.0
JXN_VALUE, JXN_LONE = 0.9, 2.8
JI_VALUE, JI_LONE = -0.7, -1.5
COM_VALUE = 1.4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    word = "" if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    prev = word
    # A token that starts with a space or punctuation begins a new word.
    if tok[:1].isspace() or not tok[:1].isalnum():
        word = tok
    else:
        word = word + tok
    lone_j = prev.strip() == "j"  # the word so far was a bare "J"
    name = re.sub(r"^\W+", "", word)  # the word without its leading space or punctuation

    if word == ".com":
        return word, COM_VALUE
    if name in NOT_NAMES:
        return word, 0.0
    if JONES.search(word) and not JONES.search(prev):
        return word, JONES_LONE if lone_j else JONES_VALUE
    if JXN.search(word) and not JXN.search(prev):
        return word, JXN_LONE if lone_j else JXN_VALUE
    if JI.search(word) and not JI.search(prev):
        return word, JI_LONE if lone_j else JI_VALUE
    return word, 0.0

"""An Italian-context spelling filter, not a word-meaning model.

Recent completed words identify Italian using dictionary frequencies. In that
context, ol/vol, double t, si, pi and cor tend positive; sc, sp, im, ed and
several other clusters tend negative. Spelling evidence fades as letters are
added to the same word. ^ marks its beginning; $ marks the current end, which
need not yet be a complete word. These few rules approximate, not memorize,
the component's varied responses to Italian word fragments.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from math import exp
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ("it", "en", "es", "fr", "pt", "ro", "de")
SPELLING_WEIGHTS = {
    'ol': 1.66,
    'u': -0.56,
    'tt': 1.41,
    'ed': -1.69,
    'sc': -0.90,
    'st': -0.78,
    'eg': -1.17,
    '^si$': 2.16,
    'im': -1.02,
    'ec': -1.54,
    '^pi$': 3.03,
    'cor': 2.02,
    'op': 1.43,
    '^al': -1.14,
    'ent': -0.82,
    'in': -0.57,
    'sp': -1.76,
    'b': -0.69,
    'es': -0.74,
    'vol': 2.26,
    'com': -1.30,
    'o': 0.20,
    'g': -0.34,
    '^re': -1.71,
    'as': -0.84,
    '^ho$': 2.23,
    '^sc': -1.82,
    '^im': -2.21,
    'ug': -1.70,
    'ond$': 1.46,
}


@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def word_evidence(word):
    return tuple(max(0.0, zipf_frequency(word, lang) - 1.5)
                 for lang in LANGUAGES)


def spelling_score(word, new_letters):
    text = "^" + word
    features = {"BIAS": 1.0}
    for width in (1, 2, 3):
        # Only the newly added letters and their immediate neighbors matter.
        first_end = max(width, len(text) - new_letters - 2)
        for end in range(first_end, len(text) + 1):
            pattern = text[end - width:end]
            strength = 0.7 ** (len(text) - end)
            features[pattern] = max(features.get(pattern, 0.0), strength)
        if len(text) >= width:
            features[text[-width:] + "$"] = 1.0
    return sum(weight * features.get(pattern, 0.0)
               for pattern, weight in SPELLING_WEIGHTS.items())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        scores, unfinished, spelling = [0.0] * len(LANGUAGES), "", ""
    else:
        _, scores, unfinished, spelling = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()

    # Decayed language evidence, updated only when a word has ended.
    for ch in token:
        if ch.isalpha():
            unfinished += ch
        else:
            if len(unfinished) >= 2:
                evidence = word_evidence(unfinished)
                strongest = max(evidence)
                if strongest >= 1.5:
                    scores = [0.93 * old + freq - strongest
                              for old, freq in zip(scores, evidence)]
            unfinished = ""
    advantage = scores[0] - max(scores[1:])
    confidence = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-max(-20.0, min(
        20.0, (advantage - 5.0) / 1.5))))

    fragment = token.strip()
    if fragment and fragment.isalpha():
        if token[0].isspace():
            spelling = ""
        spelling = (spelling + fragment)[-30:]
        value = confidence * spelling_score(spelling, len(fragment))
    else:
        spelling, value = "", 0.0
    return (doc, scores, unfinished, spelling), float(value)

The component fires on words from the semantic field of the past and of origins:
"historic", "history", "heritage", "ancient", "century", "origins", "meanings",
"legends", "mythology", "remembered", "known", "named", "inspired". Its strongest

" history", " ancient", " inspiration", so this is a "the text is about history or
origins" feature. The program is a lookup: each history word gets the average activation
it has in the training sample, and a linking preposition after a relation word gets the
average for that case. Everything else predicts 0. It is stateless: each position is
judged from its own token and the one before it.

name or entity comes:

1. Possessive markers after a noun: "Boston's", "NBC's", "Pirates'", "Ferrari's". The
   strongest cases are after a capitalised name (the next word is a name or a noun
   belonging to it). Contractions after pronouns ("it's", "he's", "let's") are off.
2. "such as" (the "as" after "such"), which introduces examples, usually names.
3. Words that introduce a name: "called", "named", "like", "including".
4. Occupation and organisation nouns that are often followed by a person or company
   name: coach, artist, producer, editor, company, firm, band, brand, party, ...
5. Japanese and Chinese attributive markers, the words that hook a modifier onto the
   noun that follows: の, 的, な, and verb/copula forms before a noun (する, した, る, ない,
   である, ...). These work like English "'s" or "of".

Everything else predicts 0. The first token of each document is a little negative.

Limits: this is a set of word lists, not a model of the context. It explains about 15
to 17% of the variance (r about 0.4). Most of the unexplained part is within-word
variation that depends on the surrounding text.
"""

READS = ()

# Pronouns whose "'s" is a contraction ("it's", "he's"), not a possessive.
PRONOUNS = {"he", "she", "it", "let", "that", "there", "who", "what", "this", "we", "you",
            "one", "everyone", "someone", "where"}

# Japanese, Chinese and Korean attributive markers (noun-modifying particles and forms).
ATTRIBUTIVE = set("の 的 之 의 한 な る する した た ない である している ている いた った 하는".split())

# Words that introduce a name or an example.
INTRODUCERS = {"called", "named", "like", "including"}

# Occupation and organisation nouns, often followed by a person or company name.
ROLES = set("""artist coach producer actor actress editor writer director company firm band brand
chain singer musician author historian player team group label party sensation platform
manufacturer scientist poet composer leader secretary defender champion winner winners
founder chef publisher illustrator businessman designer manager host minister politician
captain member cyclist spokesman mogul developer activist agency charity CEO winger guitarist""".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    cur = raw.strip()
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if same_doc else ""

    # First token of a document: slightly negative on average.
    if not same_doc:
        return carry, -0.1

    # Possessive or apostrophe attached to the previous word (no leading space).
    if cur in ("'s", "’s", "'", "’") and raw[:1] != " ":
        if prev.lower() in PRONOUNS:
            return carry, 0.0
        if not cur.endswith("s"):
            return carry, 0.15
        return carry, 1.1 if prev[:1].isupper() else 0.8

    if cur in ATTRIBUTIVE:
        return carry, 0.7
    if cur == "as" and prev == "such":
        return carry, 1.0
    if cur in INTRODUCERS:
        return carry, 0.4
    if cur in ROLES:
        return carry, 0.6
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP neuron 2653 (the down_proj component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2653).

The component's input direction is almost entirely MLP hidden unit 2653 itself, so its
activation is that unit's value. It is near zero on most tokens and matters on a few
kinds of token:

- the colon in a document's title line: "<|endoftext|>Title:" (the "Title" token is the
  first token of a new document) gives a large positive value, about 18;
- the Chinese full stop "。" gives a moderate negative value, about -0.44;
- the Chinese exclamation mark "！" gives a moderate positive value, about +0.38.

Everything else is predicted as 0. Every prediction depends only on the current token and
the two before it, so the carry is unused.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_COLON = 18.05   # ":" right after "Title", which itself follows <|endoftext|>
FULL_STOP = -0.44     # Chinese full stop 。
EXCLAMATION = 0.38    # Chinese exclamation mark ！


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    cur = toks[t]
    if cur == ":" and t >= 2 and toks[t - 1] == "Title" and toks[t - 2] == "<|endoftext|>":
        value = TITLE_COLON
    elif cur == "。":
        value = FULL_STOP
    elif cur == "！":
        value = EXCLAMATION
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Approximate negative pulses at the ends of short marked spans.

Bracket, quotation, inline-code and emphasis pulses decay with the distance
from an opening mark. Short alphabetic parentheticals get an extra pulse
if they end in a dictionary modifier or begin with a coordinator; Roman
numeral labels are excluded. Separate rules cover English 'it', German
'es', and digits completing 30/31, especially after a month name.
"""
import calendar
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
MONTHS = '|'.join(calendar.month_name[1:])
GERMAN = set(('der die das den dem des ein eine einer einen einem eines '
              'und ist sind nicht sich mit auch auf für zu im am von aus '
              'aber wie wird werden hat haben dass wenn als nur noch '
              'kann zum zur').split())
ROMANCE = set(('el la los las de del que en por para con una uno un '
               'lo le les se no il che della').split())
BRACKETS = {')': ('(', .25), '）': ('（', .34),
            ']': ('[', .14), '}': ('{', .10)}
# Opening counterpart, peak pulse and fallback when no opener was seen.
QUOTES = {'"': ('"', .78, -.30), '”': ('“', .83, -.35),
          '»': ('«', .83, -.35), '」': ('「', .83, -.35),
          "'": ("'", .52, 0), '’': ('‘', .52, 0),
          '`': ('`', .62, -.35), '*': ('*', .79, 0),
          '**': ('**', .79, 0), '$': ('$', .29, 0)}


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def modifier(word):
    tags = (wordnet.parts_of_speech(word.lower())
            | wordnet.parts_of_speech(word.lower().removeprefix('un')))
    return len(word) > 1 and not word.isupper() and bool(tags & {'adjective', 'adverb'})


def pulse(openings, mark, position, peak, missing):
    distance = position - openings.get(mark, -10000)
    if distance >= 128:
        return missing
    decay = 5 if mark == '`' else 4
    value = -peak * math.exp(-max(0, distance - 2) / decay)
    return value * .35 if distance == 1 else value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, '', {})
    _, pos, text, openings = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    q = s.strip()
    previous = text[-1:] or ' '
    value = .002
    if q in BRACKETS:
        mark, peak = BRACKETS[q]
        value = pulse(openings, mark, pos, peak, -.02 if q in (')', '）') else 0.)
        if q in (')', '）'):
            value -= .05
        if s[:1].isspace():
            value *= .4
    elif q in QUOTES:
        closing = (not s[:1].isspace() and not previous.isspace()
                   and previous not in '([{=:')
        if closing or q in ('”', '»', '」'):
            mark, peak, missing = QUOTES[q]
            value = pulse(openings, mark, pos, peak, missing)
    if s in (',”', '”,'):
        value = -.55
    elif s == ',"':
        value = -.36

    if s == ')':
        match = re.search(r'(?<!\w)\(([^()]*)$', text[-120:])
        if match and re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z -]+', match[1]):
            words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', match[1])
            if (words and len(words) <= 4
                    and not re.fullmatch(r'[ivxlcdmIVXLCDM]+', match[1])
                    and (modifier(words[-1]) or words[0].lower() in {'or', 'and', 'but'})):
                distance = pos - openings.get('(', -10000)
                value -= .35 * math.exp(-max(0, distance - 3) / 3)
    if s[-1:].isspace():
        value *= .15

    if s == ' it':
        words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', text[-40:])
        last = words[-1].lower() if words else ''
        base = set(wordnet.base_forms(last))
        value = -.08
        if last in ('what', 'whatever'):
            value = -.65
        elif 'make' in base:
            value = -.54
        elif last in ('when', 'which', 'how') or base & {'think', 'find', 'give', 'take'}:
            value = -.28
        elif last in ('if', 'and', 'but'):
            value = .02
    elif s == 'it':
        value = .10
    elif s in (' es', ' Es', 'Es'):
        words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', text[-400:].lower())
        german = sum(w in GERMAN for w in words)
        romance = sum(w in ROMANCE for w in words)
        value = -1.30 if german > romance and german > 0 else -.04
    if s in ('0', '1') and text.endswith('3'):
        value = -.30 if s == '0' else -.20
        if re.search(r'(?:' + MONTHS + r')\s+3$|月3$', text, re.I):
            value = -.85 if s == '0' else -.72

    before = previous
    for ch in s:
        if ch in '([{（“‘«「':
            openings[ch] = pos
        elif ch in '\"\'`*$' and (before.isspace() or before in '([{=:'):
            openings['**' if ch == '*' and '**' in s else ch] = pos
        before = ch
    return (doc, pos + 1, (text + s)[-500:], openings), float(value)

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 2654.

What it does: a negative-going detector for "closing" marks and one pronoun.
- Quotation marks (straight or curly double quotes, backticks, apostrophes) push the
  activation strongly negative, most of all when stuck to a preceding word.
- Closing brackets and dollar signs (")", "）", "」", "]", "$", "$$", "</") push it
  moderately negative.
- The German pronoun "es" ("ist es", "gibt es") is strongly negative.
- The English pronoun "it" is moderately negative when it follows a wh-word or a
  verb like make/have/is ("what it means", "make it easier"), and near zero otherwise.
Everything else is predicted as 0. Values are rough group means fitted on training text.
"""
READS = ()

QUOTE_MARKS = {'`': -0.5, '"': -0.45, '”': -0.5, ',"': -0.3, ',”': -0.4, "'": -0.09, ' `': -0.1}
CLOSERS = {')': -0.19, '）': -0.27, '」': -0.17, ']': -0.08, '$': -0.17, '$$': -0.15, '</': -0.13}
IT_CONTEXT = {'what', 'which', 'when', 'how', 'where', 'make', 'makes', 'making', 'made', 'have', 'has', 'is'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ''
    if tok in QUOTE_MARKS:
        return None, QUOTE_MARKS[tok]
    if tok in CLOSERS:
        return None, CLOSERS[tok]
    if tok in (' es', ' Es'):
        return None, -0.7
    if tok == ' it':
        return None, -0.45 if prev in IT_CONTEXT else -0.05
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2655: a "qing" word and "Q + acronym" detector.

Plain-language summary. This component is silent almost everywhere (it passes its
importance threshold on about 0.02% of tokens). Its large activations come from two places:

1. Chinese characters pronounced qing (清 轻 倾 傾 晴 睛 凄 慶 庆 顷 情, and words built on
   them such as 高清 and 年轻), plus the Latin spelling "Qing". These push the component
   negative. The size depends on the character: 傾 倾 晴 凄 顷 about -4.5; 轻 輕 慶 睛 高清
   不清 年轻 and "Qing" about -2.5; 清 庆 情 and 情人 and similar words about -1.2.
2. A capital Q followed by a token. An all-caps acronym after Q ("QCD", "QPM", "QTN")
   pushes the component positive (about +1.5). A digit after Q (a label such as Q4) or a
   colon after Q (a "Q:" line) pushes it negative (about -0.8 and -0.9).

On every other token the program predicts 0, the component's typical near-zero value.

What it captures: the largest and most consistent activations. What it misses: the bulk of
the variance is many small activations (under 0.3) spread across ordinary text, plus a
few rare cases. The rules explain about 7% of the variance on the eval rows (about 9-10%
on training samples). A lookup table over every token would explain more (about 27% on
held-out training rows), but it would need thousands of entries with no concept behind
them, so it is not used here.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Predicted activation on a standalone qing-sounding token, in three tiers.
QING_WORDS = {}
for _words, _value in [
    ("傾 倾 晴 凄 顷", -4.5),
    ("轻 轻轻 輕 慶 睛 高清 不清 年轻 Qing", -2.5),
    ("清 庆 情人 深情 无情 行情 情 浅 惊 驚", -1.2),
]:
    for _w in _words.split():
        QING_WORDS[_w] = _value

ACRONYM_VALUE = 1.5  # all-caps acronym (2-4 letters) right after a Q
DIGIT_VALUE = -0.8   # a number (1-2 digits) right after a Q
COLON_VALUE = -0.9   # a colon right after a Q


def _ends_with_q(text):
    """True for a Q-ending token such as "Q", " Q", "PQ" or "-Q"."""
    return text.strip().endswith("Q")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the component's activation at the last token of the prefix."""
    now = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if now in QING_WORDS:
        return carry, QING_WORDS[now]
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if same_doc and _ends_with_q(prefix.token_strings[-2]):
        if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]{2,4}", now):
            return carry, ACRONYM_VALUE
        if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]{1,2}", now):
            return carry, DIGIT_VALUE
        if now == ":":
            return carry, COLON_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Comma and list-joiner detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj, component 2656.

In plain terms, this component fires on the punctuation and conjunctions that
separate items in a list:

- The comma between list items. It is strongest inside brackets (coordinates,
  argument lists, tuples such as "(1, 2)") and after a number ("Feb 24, 2004").
  It is weak in ordinary prose and turned off after "which," "who," or "that,".
  A token that ends in a comma, such as '",' or '),', fires at about half that.
- The "and" or "or" that closes a serial list ("A, B, and C"), and "etc".
- The first token of a document (the first token of a row, or the token right
  after <|endoftext|>), where the model has no context. There it fires by how
  code-like the token is: code symbols and identifiers high, prose words low.
- Tokens that open a source file (package, #!/, /*, a triple quote, <?) fire strongly
  wherever they occur.

Everything else is near zero. The program tracks only how many brackets are
open, and resets at each document start.
"""
import re

READS = ()

FILE_OPENERS = {"package": 3.0, "#!/": 4.0, '"""\n': 3.0, "/*\n": 3.0, "<?": 3.0,
                "#include": 2.0, "#ifndef": 3.0}
RELATIVE = {"which", "who", "that"}
FUNCTION_WORDS = set("a an the of and to in is are was were be been it i he she we "
                     "they you his her their its this that with for on at as by or "
                     "from not but so".split())
OPEN, CLOSE = "([{", ")]}"


def first_token_value(s):
    """Activation of a document's first token: code-like tokens high, prose low."""
    w = s.strip()
    if s in FILE_OPENERS:
        return FILE_OPENERS[s]
    if re.search(r"[^\x00-\x7f]", w):
        return 0.0
    if re.search(r'[(){}\[\]_.:=<>/\\"#;]', s) or "\n" in s or "\t" in s:
        return 2.5
    if re.search(r"\d", s):
        return 1.6
    if w.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return -0.2
    return 0.4


def comma_value(prev, depth):
    """A comma: higher inside brackets and after a number, lower after a relative pronoun."""
    value = 0.1 + 0.7 * (depth > 0) + 0.4 * bool(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", prev))
    if prev in RELATIVE:
        value -= 0.5
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return 0, first_token_value(s)
    depth = carry or 0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    value = 0.0
    if s in FILE_OPENERS:
        value = FILE_OPENERS[s]
    elif s.strip() == ",":
        value = comma_value(prev, depth)
    elif "," in s:
        value = 0.5 * comma_value(prev, depth)
    elif s.strip() in ("and", "or") and prev == ",":
        value = 0.35
    elif s.strip() == "etc":
        value = 0.7
    depth = max(0, depth + sum(c in OPEN for c in s) - sum(c in CLOSE for c in s))
    return depth, value

    "personnel": 0.9,

    " Its": -0.9,
    " ITS": -1.6,
    "its": -0.2,

    "它们": -2.5,

End-of-text markers get a length-dependent positive value, attenuated for
Han text and sentence-ending punctuation. A document-initial 'Title:' gets
a large colon response. Smaller responses mark mixed sentence stops,
exclamations after function words, standalone forum view counts and their
following separators, and headings after long lines without final punctuation.
Only the last 200 decoded characters and the document position are retained.
"""
import math
import regex

READS = ()
HAN = regex.compile(r'\p{Script=Han}')
WORD = regex.compile(r'[A-Za-z]+$')
VIEW_COUNT = regex.compile(r'(?:^|\n)[0-9]+[km]?$')
VIEW_LINE = regex.compile(r'(?:^|\n)[0-9]+[km]? views$')
FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''
    a an the of to in for with by from at as on and or but that which
    is are was were be been it its this these those their my your his
    her our can could would should will may might must
'''.split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        age, tail, previous = 0, '', ''
    else:
        _, age, tail, previous = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if token == '<|endoftext|>':
        if age == 0:
            value = 2.38

            latin = sum(c.isascii() and c.isalpha() for c in tail)
            ending = previous.rstrip()
